title: Composition and Object Relationships
learning_outcomes: Explain the central rule or purpose of composition and object relationships using at least one correct term from the lesson.

content.intro: In this lesson, you will learn **Composition and Object Relationships** as part of **Inheritance, Interfaces, and Polymorphism**. Classes group state and behavior; primary constructors and properties keep ordinary domain models concise, while initialization order still matters. Use the subtopics—Association, Aggregation, and Composition, Has-a Versus Is-a Relationships, Modeling Dependencies Between Objects—as a checklist: predict what the example will do, then verify it in a project configured for the target platform.
content.why_it_matters: These concepts help you model domain rules and reusable APIs. Good boundaries reduce accidental mutation, unsafe casts, and code that is difficult to extend.

items.title: Association, Aggregation, and Composition
items.text: Association, Aggregation, and Composition is best learned by tracing a small collection before and after the operation. Check ordering, duplicate handling, empty inputs, and whether the API returns a new value or mutates a mutable receiver.

items.title: Has-a Versus Is-a Relationships
items.text: Has-a Versus Is-a Relationships is one part of composition and object relationships. Connect its definition to the example, identify the input/state it changes, and verify the expected behavior with a small test case.

items.title: Modeling Dependencies Between Objects
items.text: Modeling Dependencies Between Objects should support a clear object invariant: make valid states easy to represent, restrict mutation to the intended API, and keep initialization and dependencies explicit.

content_blocks.title: Common mistake to avoid
content_blocks.text: Inheritance is the default choice for sharing any behavior.
